content:
Hello!
I noticed that some important Decidable instances in core Lean depend on definitions which are not exposed, which causes the decide tactic to fail in cases which are common enough that I would expect it to work:

module

/--
error: Tactic `decide` failed for proposition
  #[1] = #[1]
because its `Decidable` instance
  #[1].instDecidableEq #[1]
did not reduce to `isTrue` or `isFalse`.

After unfolding the instance `Array.instDecidableEq`, reduction got stuck at the `Decidable` instance
  { toList := [1] }.instDecidableEqImpl { toList := [1] }
-/
#guard_msgs in
example : #[1] = #[1] := by decide
-- Problem: `Array.instDecidableEqImpl` and `Array.isEqv` are not exposed

/--
error: Tactic `decide` failed for proposition
  #v[1] = #v[1]
because its `Decidable` instance
  instDecidableEqVector #v[1] #v[1]
did not reduce to `isTrue` or `isFalse`.

After unfolding the instance `instDecidableEqVector`, reduction got stuck at the `Decidable` instance
  instDecidableEqVector.decEq #v[1] #v[1]
-/
#guard_msgs in
example : #v[1] = #v[1] := by decide
-- Problem: `instDecidableEqVector.decEq` (from `deriving`) is not exposed

/--
error: Tactic `decide` failed for proposition
  1 ∈ #[1]
because its `Decidable` instance
  Array.instDecidableMemOfLawfulBEq 1 #[1]
did not reduce to `isTrue` or `isFalse`.

After unfolding the instances `decidable_of_decidable_of_iff`, `instDecidableEqBool`,
`Array.instDecidableMemOfLawfulBEq`, and `Bool.decEq`, reduction got stuck at the `Decidable` instance
  match Array.elem 1 #[1], true with
  | false, false => isTrue ⋯
  | false, true => isFalse ⋯
  | true, false => isFalse ⋯
  | true, true => isTrue ⋯
-/
#guard_msgs in
example : 1 ∈ #[1] := by
  with_unfolding_all -- unfolding would depend on the irreducible `Array.anyM.loop`
  decide
-- Problem: `Array.elem` is not exposed, even though `Array.contains` is

Because Arrays and Vectors are common datatypes and part of core Lean, I would expect that decide works with them out-of-the-box (without resorting to native_decide), so I think that Array.isEqv, Array.elem, Array.instDecidableEqImpl, and deriving DecidableEq under the definition of Vector should be annotated with @[expose].

These are the instances I was able to find from skimming the core Lean library, although there may be more that I did not find.
They definitely should, PR with test case welcome!
